vulnerabilities.title: MX Records: 1 mail servers
vulnerabilities.description: Mail servers: mail.certifiedhacker.com

vulnerabilities.title: SPF Issues: certifiedhacker.com
vulnerabilities.description: SPF uses '?all' (neutral) — provides no protection
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use '-all' mechanism. Minimize DNS lookups. Use include for providers.

vulnerabilities.title: DKIM: 1 selectors found
vulnerabilities.description: Active selectors: default

vulnerabilities.title: DMARC Record Missing
vulnerabilities.description: No DMARC policy for certifiedhacker.com. Emails can bypass SPF/DKIM checks without any policy enforcement.

vulnerabilities.title: DNSSEC Not Configured
vulnerabilities.description: Domain certifiedhacker.com has no DNSSEC signature records. DNS responses can be forged (cache poisoning, Kaminsky attack).

vulnerabilities.title: MTA-STS not configured: certifiedhacker.com
vulnerabilities.description: No MTA-STS policy — sending servers cannot enforce TLS and may be downgraded to cleartext by an on-path attacker.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Publish an MTA-STS policy (_mta-sts TXT + https policy file).

vulnerabilities.title: Exposed MYSQL service on port 3306
Exposed POSTGRESQL service on port 5432
Unsupported / End-of-Life Software: MySQL 5.7.44
vulnerabilities.description: MySQL branches before 8.0 (e.g. 5.7) reached end of life in 2023. End-of-life software receives no security patches; treat this as a proof-of-concept for the wider estate and inventory/upgrade all affected instances.

vulnerabilities.title: Cleartext Service Exposed: FTP (port 21)
vulnerabilities.description: FTP authenticates and transfers data in cleartext, exposing credentials and files to network sniffing. Disable it and use an encrypted equivalent (SSH/SFTP/HTTPS) restricted to a management network.

vulnerabilities.title: Database Exposed to Untrusted Network: MySQL / MariaDB (port 3306)
vulnerabilities.description: A MySQL / MariaDB service is reachable on a public/routable address. Databases must never be directly exposed to untrusted networks — bind to localhost or a private management network, require authentication and TLS, and firewall the port to known application hosts only.

vulnerabilities.title: Database Exposed to Untrusted Network: PostgreSQL (port 5432)
vulnerabilities.description: A PostgreSQL service is reachable on a public/routable address. Databases must never be directly exposed to untrusted networks — bind to localhost or a private management network, require authentication and TLS, and firewall the port to known application hosts only.
